cards.text: This psalm is from David, the shepherd who became Israel's king. It's for anybody who's ever watched someone do wrong and get AHEAD for it, like the coworker who skips every step and STILL gets the corner office. David starts right there: don't fret over people who do evil.

cards.question: David says don't fret over people who do evil. What's the other thing he tells you not to do about people who do wrong?
Why not fret over evildoers? David says they ___ quickly like grass.

cards.text: So what do you do INSTEAD of fretting? David's list: trust in the LORD, do good, dwell in the land, cultivate faithfulness, and NOWHERE on it does it say stare at their vacation photos and get mad.

cards.question: Then David says to delight yourself in the LORD. What does he say the LORD will give you?

cards.text: Next: commit your way to the LORD, trust in Him, and He will do it. Then David paints a picture: the LORD will bring forth your righteousness like the dawn, your justice like the noonday sun.

cards.question: David says the LORD will bring out your righteousness like the dawn and your justice like the noonday sun. What's the picture?

answers.text: It will shine out for all to see
It will stay hidden until evening
It will fade as the day goes on

cards.text: Then comes the hard one: be still before the LORD and wait patiently for Him. I had YEARS in a junk drawer to practice waiting, and I STILL stand at the oven window like the cookies owe me money.

cards.question: David says to refrain from anger and abandon wrath, because fretting can only bring ___.

cards.text: And here's why you can let it go: the evildoers will be cut off. That's not your job, friend, so put the rolling pin DOWN.

cards.question: True or false: David says the people who hope in the LORD will inherit the land.

cards.text: Then David says: yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more. A LITTLE while, friend, not one of those 'between 8 and 6' delivery windows.

cards.question: True or false: David says that after that little while, if you go looking for the wicked, you'll still find them hanging around.
Once the wicked are gone, who does David say will inherit the land and delight in abundant prosperity?

cards.text: Now David shows what the wicked are up to: they scheme against the righteous and gnash their teeth at them. Gnashing teeth, friend, that's the face of a man who just opened his electric bill.

cards.question: The wicked gnash their teeth at the righteous, but the Lord ___, seeing that their day is coming.

cards.text: And it gets serious. The wicked draw the sword and bend the bow to bring down the poor and needy and to slay those whose ways are upright.

cards.question: The wicked have their swords drawn against the upright. What does David say happens to those swords?

answers.text: They are taken by the king

cards.text: Next David compares the righteous who have a little with the wicked who have a lot. Now, I came home from that bakery bin with a 25-cent price sticker, so you KNOW I'm leaning in for this one.

cards.question: True or false: David says the little that the righteous have is better than the abundance of many who are wicked.

cards.text: Why? Because the arms of the wicked will be broken, but the LORD upholds the righteous.

cards.question: David says the LORD knows the days of the blameless. How long does he say their inheritance will last?

cards.text: And when hard times hit? In the time of evil they won't be ashamed, and in the days of famine they'll be satisfied.

cards.question: David says the wicked and enemies of the LORD will vanish and fade away like ___.

cards.text: The wicked borrow and don't repay, but the righteous are gracious and giving. We ALL know that guy who says he'll pay you back Friday and never says WHICH Friday.
Those the LORD blesses will inherit the land, but the cursed will be destroyed.

cards.question: True or false: David says the LORD orders a man's steps but takes no interest in his journey.
Even when that man falls, David says he won't be overwhelmed. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD is holding his hand
He always lands on his feet

cards.text: Then David gets personal. He says, "I once was young and now am old, yet never have I seen the righteous abandoned or their children begging for bread."

cards.question: David says the righteous are ever generous and quick to lend. What does he say about their children?

cards.text: David's advice now is simple: turn away from evil and do good, so you will abide forever.

cards.question: David gives a reason to turn from evil and do good. What does he say the LORD loves?

cards.text: The LORD won't forsake His saints, and the righteous will inherit the land and dwell in it forever. That's "inherit the land" AGAIN, friend, and when somebody repeats himself THAT much, it goes on a sticky note on the fridge.

cards.question: Now David describes the righteous man. What does David say comes out of his mouth?
David says the righteous man's steps do not falter. What does he say is in that man's heart?

cards.text: But the wicked lie in wait for the righteous and seek to slay them.

cards.question: True or false: David says the LORD will leave the righteous in the power of the wicked who are lying in wait for them.

cards.text: So David says: wait for the LORD and keep His way, and He'll raise you up to inherit the land. When the wicked are cut off, you'll see it.
Then David says he has seen a wicked, ruthless man flourishing like a well-rooted native tree. Big. Rooted. Not going ANYWHERE.

cards.question: David saw a wicked man flourishing like a well-rooted tree. What happened to that man?

answers.text: He passed away and was no more
He turned from his wicked ways
He grew richer than ever before

cards.text: Now David says to consider the blameless and observe the upright. Watch THEM, friend, not the guy with the flashy car and the shady paperwork.

cards.question: David says to consider the blameless and observe the upright. What does he say awaits the man of peace?

cards.text: But the transgressors will all be destroyed, and the future of the wicked will be cut off.

cards.question: The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD, and He is their ___ in time of ___.
In the last line, David says the LORD helps the righteous and rescues them from the wicked. Why does He save them?

answers.text: Because they take refuge in Him

findings.problem: The question makes fretting the reason to refrain from anger and abandon wrath ('refrain from anger and abandon wrath, because fretting can only bring ___'). In Psalm 37:8, 'it can only bring harm' is attached to 'do not fret', not to refraining from anger. The card adds a connection the text doesn't make, and it drops the 'do not fret' command itself.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Story card 12 has already told the baker 'the wicked will be no more' (Psalm 37:10a). That gives away the answer to this true or false question about whether the wicked will still be found.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Once the wicked are gone' turns the contrast in Psalm 37:11 ('But the meek will inherit the land') into a sequence in time. The text doesn't order these two things.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Even when that man falls' points back to the man in card 13's question, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say who he is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 3: 6 of its 8 choice cards are multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 5, 10, 12 and 15), against 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
